VIDEO LAB

WHERE THE LIGHT COMES FROM - the switch decides:
  detect (tracked) - Flare Track follows the brightest spot. The
     picker's light handle greys out, because tracking owns it.
     detect_max_lights caps how many FLARES exist, not how many
     candidates are looked at, so a busy shot (dappled light in
     trees) cannot spawn a second flare across the frame. If it
     locks onto the wrong light, set search_radius above 0 and put
     search_u/search_v on the one you want - the overlay draws a
     cyan ring showing where it is allowed to look.
  keyframes        - Flare Keyframes drives BOTH points by hand:
     light_keys and anchor_keys, each 'frame: u,v; frame: u,v'.
  manual           - nothing is passed on, so Flare Render uses its
     own picker: drag the light and the anchor where you want them.
The anchor (cyan) always follows flare_x/flare_y unless keyframed.

1. Pick a video in Load Video. Frames flow as one batch.
2. Flare Track gives stable ids, smoothed positions, fade in/out and
   velocity coasting through moments the detector loses the light.
   The overlay preview shows the tracked points per frame.
3. Depth Anything + Flare Depth Adapter (temporal_smooth) drive
   occlusion; occlusion_smooth on Flare Render (gear panel) spreads
   any hard occlusion cut into a fade across frames.
4. The flare animates itself as the light moves - no keyframes:
   - rows with a RED EDGE in the editor carry a trigger rule.
     Anamorphic Gold's edge gleam blooms as the light nears the frame
     border. Twirl a row open and hit 'show' under preview region to
     paint the trigger area over the picker.
   - lens (global row): flicker gives every tracked light its own
     brightness wobble; edge fade cuts a light that leaves frame.
   - scene_color (gear panel) tints each flare by the plate colour at
     the light, so a warm street lamp flares warm.
5. Both video outputs: composite and the flare pass over black for
   external compositing.
